#library
```{r}
remotes::install_github("evo-palaeo/TeachingMaterials")
install.packages("tidyverse")
install.packages("ggplot2")
library(TeachingMaterials)
library(ggplot2)
library(ape)
library(cluster)
```

#Load data_ sequnece before alignment
```{r}
bacteria <- read.dna(
  "../data/processed/combined.fasta",
  format = "fasta"
)

bacteria
sapply(bacteria, length)
```
#aligned_sequnece
#MUSCLE on phylogency.fr were used to perform sequence alignment since there are 100 sequences and the limit of A la carte mode is 50
```{r}
bacteria_aligned <- read.dna(
  "../data/processed/aligned_sequences.aln",
  format = "fasta"
)
bacteria_aligned
nrow(bacteria_aligned) 
ncol(bacteria_aligned) 

#visualising it
image(
  bacteria_aligned,
  show.labels = FALSE,
  show.nucs = FALSE)
#It is worth noting that alignemnts were not trimmed since only MUSCLE was used
#this however keeps all the information that could be useful
```

#Raw distances
```{r}
raw_distances<-dist.dna(
 bacteria_aligned,
  model = "raw",
 pairwise.deletion = TRUE #ignore gap rich ends in sequence 
 # only sites that have bases in each sequences are compared
)
as.matrix(raw_distances)[1:3, 1:3]
# data is now stored in DNAbin matrix instead of list since it is now aligned
```
#JC69 distances
```{r}
jc_dist <- dist.dna(
  bacteria_aligned,
  model = "JC69",
  pairwise.deletion = TRUE
)

summary(jc_dist)
```

#graph to compare jcdistance and raw distance: why jcdistance is used
```{r}
plot(
  as.vector(raw_distances),
  as.vector(jc_dist),
  pch = 1,
  cex = 0.5,
  xlab = "Raw genetic distance",
  ylab = "JC69-corrected distance",
  main = "Comparison of Raw and JC69 Distances"
)


abline(a = 0, b = 1, col = "red", lty = 2)

cor(as.vector(jc_dist),as.vector(raw_distances))
max(as.vector(raw_distances))

distance_difference <- as.vector(jc_dist) -
                       as.vector(raw_distances)

summary(distance_difference)
```
#Perform PCoA
```{r}
pcoa_result <- cmdscale(
  jc_dist,
  k = 10,
  eig = TRUE
)
```

#metadata for plotting, seperating the outlets
```{r}
diff_outlets<-data.frame(Sequence = rownames(bacteria_aligned),
  outlet = sub("_seq.*$", "", rownames(bacteria_aligned)))
head (diff_outlets)
table(diff_outlets$outlet) #shows number of sequences in each outlet
```
#PCoA coordinates
```{r}
pcoa_df <- as.data.frame(pcoa_result$points)
colnames(pcoa_df) <- paste0("PCoA", seq_len(ncol(pcoa_df)))
eig <- pcoa_result$eig
variance <- 100 * eig / sum(eig[eig > 0])
variance[1:10]
pcoa_df$Sequence <- rownames(pcoa_df)
# linking different food outlet to coordinates
pcoa_df$outlet <- diff_outlets$outlet[
  match(pcoa_df$Sequence, diff_outlets$Sequence)]
head(pcoa_df)
```
#plotting PCoA figure
```{r}
library(ggplot2)

p1 <- ggplot(
  pcoa_df,aes(x = PCoA1, y = PCoA2, colour = outlet)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(
    x = paste0("PCoA1 (", round(variance[1], 1), "%)"),
    y = paste0("PCoA2 (", round(variance[2], 1), "%)"),
    title = "PCoA of Bacterial DNA Sequences",
    colour = "Food outlet"
  ) +
  theme_classic()

p1
#plotting PCoA3 against PCoA4
p2 <- ggplot(
  pcoa_df,
  aes(x = PCoA3, y = PCoA4, colour = outlet)
) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(
    x = paste0("PCoA3 (", round(variance[3], 1), "%)"),
    y = paste0("PCoA4 (", round(variance[4], 1), "%)"),
    title = "PCoA: Axes 3 and 4",
    colour = "Food outlet"
  ) +
  theme_classic()

p2
round(variance[1:4], 2) #shows how many % each plot represents
```


#k-means clusttering
```{r}
pcoa_coords <- pcoa_df[, paste0("PCoA", 1:10)] #extract PCoA axes
set.seed(123) #setting it here so its reproducible 
km <- kmeans(
  pcoa_coords,
 centers = 3,
  nstart = 25)

# Store the cluster assignments
pcoa_df$Cluster <- factor(km$cluster)
pcoa_df$Cluster
```

#silhouette analysis
```{r}
set.seed(123)
k_values <- 2:10
mean_silhouette <- numeric(length(k_values))

for (i in seq_along(k_values)) {

  km_test <- kmeans(
    pcoa_coords,
    centers = k_values[i],
    nstart = 25
  )

  sil <- silhouette(km_test$cluster, dist(pcoa_coords))

  mean_silhouette[i] <- mean(sil[, "sil_width"])
}

# Plot the results
plot(
  k_values,
  mean_silhouette,
  type = "b",
  pch = 19,
  xlab = "Number of clusters (k)",
  ylab = "Mean silhouette width",
  main = "Choosing the Number of Clusters"
)
```
#optimal number of clustering
```{r}
set.seed(123)
optimal_k <- k_values[which.max(mean_silhouette)]
km_optimal <- kmeans(
  pcoa_coords,
  centers = optimal_k,
  nstart = 25
)
pcoa_df$Clusters <- factor(km_optimal$cluster)
optimal_k
```

#plotting the cluster on the two PcoA axes
```{r}
km_optimal$cluster #see which cluster each DNA sequence belongs to 

ggplot(pcoa_df, aes(x = PCoA1, y = PCoA2, colour = Clusters)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.9) +
  labs(
    x = paste0("PCoA1 (", round(variance[1], 1), "%)"),
    y = paste0("PCoA2 (", round(variance[2], 1), "%)"),
    title = "K-means Clustering of Bacterial DNA Sequences",
    colour = "Cluster") +
  theme_classic()

```
#how bacterial sequence groups are distributed across eight different food outlets
```{r}
outlet_groups <- table(
  pcoa_df$outlet,
  pcoa_df$Clusters)

outlet_groups
#percentage of each outlet's sequence in each cluster
round(prop.table(outlet_groups, margin = 1) * 100,1)
```
#identifying representative from each cluster using a medoid model
```{r}
distance_matrix <- as.matrix(jc_dist)#converts jc69 distances into matrix
representatives <- character(length(levels(pcoa_df$Clusters)))
names(representatives) <- levels(pcoa_df$Clusters)

for (group in levels(pcoa_df$Clusters)) { 
  members <- pcoa_df$Sequence[pcoa_df$Clusters == group] # Finds all sequences in that cluster

  #distances between clusters
  cluster_dist <- distance_matrix[
    members,members, #compare two clusters
    drop = FALSE]

  total_distances <- rowSums(cluster_dist) #distance for each seq

  # sequence with the smallest total distance
  representatives[group] <- members[which.min(total_distances)]
  }

representatives
```


#extarcting the representatives!
```{r}
bacteria_original <- read.dna(
  "../data/processed/combined.fasta",
  format = "fasta")

stopifnot(all(representatives %in% names(bacteria_original)))
#check if seq in representatives can be found in bacteria_original

representative_dna <- bacteria_original[representatives] #extract representative sequences from bacteria_original using id in "representatives"

representative_dna
```
#export 5 representatives as fasta 
```{r}
write.dna(
  representative_dna,
  file = "../data/processed/representatives.fasta",
  format = "fasta",
  nbcol = -1,
  colsep = "")
```
